FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or project context correctly. In `bench/endocrine.py`, the target file is copied to a temp dir under `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`, but post-fix analysis runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that lone file only. For modules like `bench/endocrine.py` that import `bench.dm._types`, the temp file is no longer inside the `bench/` package and no project tree/config is copied. That means pyright and potentially other tools evaluate a different environment than the real codebase, producing import errors or different results unrelated to the fix itself. This breaks the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” capability on the happy path for package modules.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluation verdicts become systematically misleading for findings on package-scoped files: a good fix can be marked HARMFUL due to artificial missing-import/type-resolution failures, and a bad fix can be marked SAFE because only the isolated file is checked without its real package neighbors or config. These verdicts feed the immune pipeline Stage 4 via `evaluate_fixes()`, which marks findings `verified=True` for SAFE/NEUTRAL. That crosses the interface into `immune_agents.py` and activates the bug-closed gate in later rounds, so false SAFE/NEUTRAL decisions can prematurely close real bugs, while false HARMFUL decisions can block valid fixes from ever being verified.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — preserve the original relative path inside the sandbox and run tools from a sandbox root that contains the package layout needed by the file. For example, create `tmpdir/bench/...`, copy the target file to its original relative path under that root, and run post-fix tool checks against that sandboxed path with `cwd=tmpdir` so imports and package structure resolve as in the real project, while still not modifying source.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can execute tests against the wrong code. It writes only the patched target file into a temp directory, then runs `_run_tool(test_cmd, ..., cwd=tmpdir)`. The provided test command is not rewritten to reference the patched file or a sandboxed project tree. In the documented integration from `immune_agents.py`, the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`; from `cwd=tmpdir`, that path usually does not exist, and even if tests resolve via an absolute/project path, they run against the original repository, not the patched sandbox copy. So `tests_passed` does not reliably measure the proposed fix.
FOLLOW: This contaminates fix verdicts in both directions. If tests fail because the test path is missing in tmpdir, valid fixes are marked HARMFUL. If tests pass by discovering tests in the original repo, the patched file is not actually under test, so unsafe fixes can be marked SAFE. Because `_compute_fix_verdict()` treats `tests_passed is False` as HARMFUL and `tests_passed is True` with zero net issues as SAFE, the verdict becomes detached from sandbox reality. Through the endocrine→immune interface, these false verdicts drive `verified=True`, which then changes relay summaries and NK duplicate closure behavior across rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — only run tests against a sandbox that contains the project layout the test command expects. Copy the minimal project subtree needed for the target module and tests into tmpdir, patch the sandboxed file there, and execute the test command against sandbox-relative paths. If that setup is not available, skip tests and leave `tests_passed=None` instead of running misleading tests.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses an aggregate sum of net issues: `total_net = result.net_type_errors + result.net_ruff_errors + result.net_bandit_issues`; it returns HARMFUL only if `total_net > 0` and SAFE if `total_net < 0`. This lets a fix that introduces new issues in one tool but removes more in another be labelled SAFE overall. Example: `+2` bandit issues, `-3` ruff issues yields `total_net = -1` ⇒ SAFE, despite introducing new security defects. The docstring says “HARMFUL: new issues introduced,” which this implementation violates.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the endocrine layer can certify regressions as SAFE/NEUTRAL and the immune pipeline will mark those findings `verified=True`. That is especially serious because the three tracked dimensions are not fungible: introducing a new bandit issue is not cancelled out by reducing style violations. Once marked verified, the bug-closed gate suppresses further reports of the same issue, so the system can lock in a regressive fix and stop reviewing it.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive net in any tracked tool as HARMFUL: if `net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`, return HARMFUL. Only return SAFE when at least one net is negative and none are positive; otherwise keep the existing no-change logic.
VERIFIED: TRUE

CONFIRM C0001 — `scan_health()` misreports missing tools as available. Evidence: each runner returns `[]` on `"NOT_FOUND"`, and `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally.

CONFIRM C0021 — timeout handling is also misclassified as healthy/no-findings. Evidence: `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but runners only special-case `"NOT_FOUND"`; they then parse empty output and silently return `[]`.

CONFIRM C0029 — `run_pyright()` can miss diagnostics when JSON is emitted on `stderr`. Evidence: it parses only `result.stdout` and ignores `stderr` except for exact `"NOT_FOUND"`.

EXTEND C0004 | The same availability bug affects timeouts as well as missing binaries: a timed-out tool returns no diagnostics and is still marked available/healthy by `scan_health()`, so the brain cannot distinguish “clean code” from “tool never completed”.

CONFIRM C0005 — several advertised endocrine capabilities never fire. Evidence inside target file: CrossHair and Python 3.13 binary constants are declared but unused; no defect-detection pass exists beyond per-tool categorisation; no explicit dead-code/race/off-by-one detector beyond minimal tag mapping.

CONFIRM C0030 — severity normalization is inconsistent. Evidence: pyright passes through raw severities, ruff hardcodes every issue to `"warning"`, bandit maps LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH to info/warning/error, mypy preserves raw severities including `"note"`; cross-tool aggregate severity counts are therefore not comparable.

CONFIRM C0006 — `health_trend()` returns ragged histories. Evidence: it appends counts only for categories present in each scan, so absent categories do not get explicit zeros for that round.
